newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Eight jet, diesel arbitrage cargoes headed to Asia.
newsitem.headline: Eight jet, diesel arbitrage cargoes headed to Asia.

text.p: Firm gas oil and jet fuel prices in Singapore have opened an arbitrage for the export of up to eight spot cargoes to Asia from the west, traders said on Thursday.
The arbitrage opened some time last week following the steep fall in gas oil and heating oil prices in the west against a relatively stable Singapore swaps market, they said.
The east-west gas oil spread blew up to a wide $15 per tonne in favour of the east earlier this month against a spread of $20.50 in favour of the west in early October.
Traders said that one gas oil cargo from North West Europe and two cargoes from the Mediterranean were fixed for India for arrival in December.
On top of this, they said one gas oil and one to two jet fuel cargoes from the U.S. west coast and two jet fuel cargoes from Venezuela were expected to be shipped to Japan and India.
Traders said they do not expect further exports from the west as prices there have risen.
"The arbitrage is now closed," one trader said.
In London overnight, November gas oil futures on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) rose $7.00 per tonne to $215.00. The contract expires November 12.
NYMEX December heating oil rose 1.03 cent to 66.45 cent in New York before adding another 0.45 cent in ACCESS trading to 66.90 cents per gallon.
The firmer tone followed stock data from the American Petroleum Institute and Energy Information Administration showing a decline in national distillate stocks.
Traders said talk of exports of Russian gas oil from Ventspils to the east has died down due to the rising prices on the IPE.
